result.strongest_objection: The doc never demonstrates that the rule it relaxes is what stands between the fleet and a record, because it cannot produce a single verified fire that would record under the new rules. The only two degraded fires it actually examined (world 369/370, V10) are admitted in Risks to STILL be barred under D2 (D-WORLD-113 exists only on the branch, V12; rows 150/151 wait on an attended step and an external predicate). The generalizing premise 'Every live World fire since its queue became fully human-gated has fallen back somewhere' rests on n=2 sampled iterations, and stapledon's fires were never read (its own 'Not verified' section). Worst, the observation criterion is unfalsifiable: it is satisfied by 'each report shows which D2 or D1 bar fired,' which is operationally identical to today's status quo (reports already say NOT recorded, V10) — the change can land, add five mutants, change nothing, and still be declared a success. A design whose entire measurable benefit is conjectural and whose success criterion passes on a no-op fails premise verification.
result.catch: Three things to fix or verify: (1) The crux term of D1(a)/(b) — 'every gate the no-pick path runs' vs gates 'the no-pick path skips by design' — is defined nowhere; no V-row cites a canonical no-pick gate list in the skill or driver, so the replacement bar's central distinction is unverifiable controller judgement with no enumerated referent (wording tests T1-T5 cannot touch it). (2) V19 never exercised the rc-1 fallback to br=dev, and the claim that the block 'mirrors idle-fingerprint.sh lines 61-68' is asserted without quoting those lines; the hardcoded 'dev' fallback is verified only for world (origin/dev exists), not for stapledon or any other mission whose default branch may differ. (3) The unsupported universal claim about every world fire falling back, and the absence of any retro-application of D1/D2 to the 8 COMPLETED fires in V11 to show at least one would have recorded.
result.proposed_fix: 1) Add a V-row that retro-applies D1/D2 to the last 10 no-pick fires for BOTH world and stapledon (read stapledon's reports; trace whether rows 150/151's attended step maps to an OPEN row), and state explicitly which fires, if any, would have recorded. If zero would have, re-scope the doc to say so and justify landing a wording change with no qualifying case, or do not land. 2) Make the observation criterion falsifiable: 'within the first 10 world/stapledon fires after landing, at least one mission-<name>-idle-fingerprint file is promoted AND followed by a verdict=IDLE elapsed_s=0 slot row; if none, the change is treated as no-op and re-evaluated' — with the retro-analysis from (1) as the stated baseline prediction. 3) Replace D1(a)/(b)'s undefined gate set with a cited canonical list (quote the skill section or driver line range enumerating no-pick gates in a new V-row); if no such list exists, define it in this same edit. 4) Add a V-row quoting idle-fingerprint.sh lines 61-68 to substantiate the 'mirrors' claim, exercise the rc-1 origin/HEAD-absent path in the /tmp block test (temp clone without origin/HEAD), and either verify the 'dev' fallback branch exists for every covered mission or replace it with a derived default (e.g. remote HEAD) / fail closed.

result.strongest_objection: The proposed ledger-proof block silently discards the exit status of mission_decisions.sh. Its output is piped through cut and captured without checking success. If the parser emits the cited OPEN ids and then fails, the block can still print OK for every id, with none of the documented conditions barring recording. This contradicts D1(b)'s failed-read bar and the no-silent-fallback axiom.
result.catch: V19 tests a failed workdir, not a failed ledger parser. The wording mutants also cannot detect this fail-open behavior. Checking that cited ids appear in stdout is not verification that the ledger read completed successfully.
result.proposed_fix: Capture and check the parser invocation separately before extracting ids: `if ! rows=$(bash "$MISSION_DRIVER_ROOT/scripts/mission_decisions.sh" --open --file "$t"); then echo 'LEDGER READ FAILED: do not record'; rm -f "$t"; exit 1; fi`, then derive `open` from the successfully captured output. Make every prerequisite failure terminate the proof block unsuccessfully. Add executable tests for parser failure with empty stdout and, critically, parser failure after emitting all requested ids; both must produce a READ FAILED marker and must not produce an eligible proof. Add the resulting commands and observations to the verification log.

result.strongest_objection: The replacement bash snippet leaves the tempfile behind if `symbolic-ref` fails in a way that leaves `br` unset, though `rm -f "$t"` runs at the end of the snippet anyway because of `;` chaining; more importantly, if `mission_decisions.sh --open --file "$t"` itself fails or errors out while `br` is non-empty, the subshell exits non-zero, `open` is empty, and it reports `open rows: 0` without flagging a script failure versus legitimately zero open rows (though both bar the record).
result.catch: In the replacement bash block, `for id in D-X-1 D-X-2; do ...` uses literal placeholder IDs (`D-X-1 D-X-2`). Verify that controllers won't copy-paste the literal placeholders instead of substituting their actual cited IDs, or make the placeholder syntax more obviously a template (e.g., `<CITED-ID-1> ...`).
result.proposed_fix: In the replacement text's bash block, change `for id in D-X-1 D-X-2; do` to `for id in <CITED-ID-1> <CITED-ID-2>; do` (and adjust T1-T4 if any test checks that line) so a literal copy-paste fails loudly with a syntax redirect error rather than silently printing `MISS D-X-1`.
